problem:
What is the variance of the following data set?

$$
-12,\,-14,\,-7,\,11,\,-15,\,5,\,0,\,-8,\,-14
$$

Do not round your answer.

${\sigma }^{2}=$
{{field-1}}
worked_solution:
If we have a data set that consists of the points ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n},$ then the variance can be computed as

$$
{\sigma }^{2}=\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}-(\overset{―}{x})^{2},
$$

where $\overset{―}{x}$ is the mean of the data set and $\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}$ is the mean of the squares of the points in the data set.

First, let's compute $\overset{―}{x}.$ There are $n=9$ points in our data set, so the mean is

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{x} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{9}\cdot (-12-14-7+11-15+5+0-8-14) \\  & =\frac{1}{9}\cdot (-54) \\  & =-6.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, let's compute $\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}.$ Computing the mean of the squares of the points in the data set, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{{x}^{2}} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{9}\cdot ((-12)^{2}+(-14)^{2}+(-7)^{2}+{11}^{2}+(-15)^{2}+{5}^{2}+{0}^{2}+(-8)^{2}+(-14)^{2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{9}\cdot (144+196+49+121+225+25+0+64+196) \\  & =\frac{1}{9}\cdot 1020 \\  & =\frac{1020}{9} \\  & =\frac{340}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the variance is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }^{2} & =\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}-(\overset{―}{x})^{2} \\  & =\frac{340}{3}-{(-6)}^{2} \\  & =\frac{340}{3}-36 \\  & =\frac{340-108}{3} \\  & =\frac{232}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
